meta.title: oscp tmux — this machine's terminal
meta.note: Ctrl-a on this page is one custom prefix, chosen for ease. Anyone can set their own. A line that starts with $ is a shell command. A key table is pressed inside tmux, not pasted into the shell.
meta.flow: prefix Ctrl-a  →  a key, or Ctrl-a then : for a command

sections.name: The config in ~/.tmux.conf
sections.goal: Mouse on, prefix Ctrl-a, 50000 lines of scrollback, logging on Ctrl-a H.
steps: drop the default prefix. unbind is short for unbind-key
prefix is Ctrl-a. set is short for set-option
Ctrl-a a sends a real Ctrl-a to the program
Ctrl-a H toggles the live log
bind H if-shell -F '#{pane_pipe}' 'pipe-pane ; display-message "Logging OFF"' 'pipe-pane -o "cat >> ~/tmux_live.log 2>/dev/null" ; display-message "Logging ON"'
Ctrl-a C stops logging and empties the file
bind C pipe-pane \; run-shell "> ~/tmux_live.log" \; display-message "Cleared log and forced logging OFF"
reload the file after you edit it. source is the same command
sections.why: These six blocks are the whole file. oscp tmux does not rewrite ~/.tmux.conf.

sections.name: Live log — Ctrl-a H and Ctrl-a C
sections.goal: The pane's output is appended to ~/tmux_live.log. One copy. That is the feature.
steps: turn logging on, or off if it is already on
Ctrl-a then H. The status line says Logging ON or Logging OFF.
read the log from a different pane or a different terminal
stop the pipe on this pane from the shell. pipep is the same command
Ctrl-a then C: logging off, and the file is emptied
Do: turn logging on before the work you want to keep.
Do: run ls, shells, and tools in that pane as usual.
Do: read ~/tmux_live.log from another pane or another terminal.
Do: Ctrl-a H again when you are finished.
Don't: cat, tail -f, less, or vim the log in the pane that is logging.
Don't: grep the log file from that same pane. ls | grep tmux is fine — it does not print the log.
Don't: expect Ctrl-a C to stop a cat that is already running. Ctrl-C first, then Ctrl-a C.
sections.gotcha: cat ~/tmux_live.log inside the logged pane prints the file, the logger appends that print, and cat prints the new part too. A few commands become tens of megabytes. tail -f in that same pane is the same loop.

sections.name: Prefix, then a key or a colon
sections.goal: Ctrl-a is the prefix. The next key is a tmux action. Ctrl-a then : opens the command prompt.
steps: Ctrl-a, then a key from oscp tmux keys.
Ctrl-a, then : — type a command, Tab completes, Enter runs it.
Ctrl-a, then a — send Ctrl-a through to the shell (start of line).
sections.why: Until ~/.tmux.conf is loaded, the prefix is still Ctrl-b. tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf makes it Ctrl-a.

sections.name: Prefix keys (after Ctrl-a)
sections.goal: Press Ctrl-a, release, then the key. These are not shell commands.

rows: zoom this pane to the full window
turn this pane into its own window
enter copy mode: scroll, select, copy
paste the tmux buffer into this pane

sections.why: Mouse is on, so clicking a pane, dragging a border, and scrolling the wheel work too.

sections.name: Command prompt — Ctrl-a then :
sections.goal: Commands typed after the prefix, then a colon. This config is Ctrl-a, then colon, then the command. Default prefix is Ctrl-b. No parentheses means that command has no short name.
steps: every command and its short name. lscm is the same command
every key. lsk is the same command
the options this config set. show is the same command

rows: every command and its short name; Tab completes either
end that session. No short name
this pane becomes its own window
type the same keys into every pane
stop the live log on this pane
enter copy mode (same as prefix [). No short name
write the buffer to a file
read a file into the buffer
copy keys: Ctrl-Space, then Alt-w (the default)
copy all scrollback into the paste buffer
a clock; q leaves it. No short name
sessions, windows, and panes in one list. No short name

sections.why: Ctrl-a ? is the key list. list-commands (lscm) is every command. source-file and source are one command, and the same is true of every pair above. The short name works after Ctrl-a : and after tmux in the shell.

sections.name: The same actions from the shell
sections.goal: tmux <command> works outside a session, and inside one. The comment names the other spelling. Either spelling runs.
sections.why: source and source-file reload ~/.tmux.conf. New panes pick up the prefix only after that reload. The copied line is one valid command; the comment is the other name.

sections.name: Copy mode and paste
sections.goal: Ctrl-a then [ enters copy mode. You scroll, select, and copy into tmux's paste buffer. Ctrl-a then ] pastes that buffer into the pane.
steps: 1. Enter. Ctrl-a then [. You are no longer typing into the shell.
2. Move. Arrows. Ctrl-p and Ctrl-n go up and down. Ctrl-b and Ctrl-f go left and right. PageUp and PageDown. Alt-< is the top of the history, Alt-> the bottom.
3. Select. Ctrl-Space starts the selection. Move to the other end. R toggles a rectangle.
4. Copy. Alt-w or Ctrl-w copies the selection and leaves copy mode. Ctrl-k copies from the cursor to the end of the line.
5. Paste. Ctrl-a then ] inserts the buffer at the cursor.
Leave without copying: q, Escape, or Ctrl-c. Ctrl-g drops the selection and stays in copy mode.
Search while inside: Ctrl-r up, Ctrl-s down. n repeats, N reverses.
Mouse is on: drag to select, release to copy. Double-click a word, triple-click a line. The wheel scrolls.
list what was copied. short name: lsb
print the newest buffer. short name: showb
write the buffer to a file. short name: saveb
read a file into the buffer. short name: loadb
paste from the shell. short name: pasteb
optional vi keys. full name: set-option

rows: left / right. Ctrl-b is not the prefix in here
start of line / end of line. Ctrl-a is not the prefix in here
a page. Space also pages down
copy to the end of the line and leave
drop the selection, stay in copy mode
paste, once you have left copy mode

sections.why: Stock tmux and this config use emacs keys (mode-keys emacs). Space pages down. Selection starts at Ctrl-Space. Vi keys are a setting, set -g mode-keys vi: Space starts the selection and Enter copies. Prefix ] pastes tmux's buffer into the pane. The terminal clipboard is separate: Cmd-V on a Mac, Ctrl-Shift-V in many Linux terminals.
sections.gotcha: Alt-w fills the tmux buffer and also asks the terminal to update its clipboard (set-clipboard is external by default). If that clipboard stays empty, Ctrl-a ] still pastes inside the pane, and tmux save-buffer writes a file. history-limit 50000 is how far the scroll goes back.
